items.title: 52115_Danny Barker oral history interview
items.q: Perry Bradford recorded the first Blues singer... Bradford played, but not too much. He was a great composer.

ctx.x: Old Perry Bradford handled them for a while, didn't he.
Perry Bradford recorded the first Blues singer, which was Mamie...
The first Black woman on record.

items.title: Danny Barker — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

ctx.x: Me and him were tight. I’d worked with James P. Johnson. I was tight with him. James P. Johnson . . . At that time I was working with James P. Johnson before I joined Benny Carter. Between Cab. James P. Johnson heard the record, Don’t You Feel My Legs, say, “You got a hit. I’m working with you.” He said . . . I said, “Yeah.” He said, “Yeah, but bring your vasoline.” I said, “Bring my vasoline for what?” He said, “Because you’re going to get screwed.” [? (inaudible)] know what that mean. He wrote The Charleston,…

keys—they do that, piano players, when they’re playing—raise my hand. Don’t touch a note. Then come right in. He said, “I never seen nobody do that. That’s what you call respect.” And I gets that from “The Lion” in front of a gang of people. Not a gang of people. About six critical musicians.
